text:
liam_arch: RFC follow-up: proposing an "edge-lite" model for private control plane. keep a single global control-plane datastore, but create tiny per-tenant proxies inside customer VPCs for certing, onboarding hooks, and route/ENI programming. thoughts on tradeoffs?

emma_infra: sounds like a middle ground between full peering and centralized relay. so control-plane logic remains central, proxies do the AWS-specific ops?

liam_arch: exactly. central CP issues desired state, proxy reconciles in-customer (routes, ENIs, cert requests) and reports ops/events. proxies are ephemeral to reduce attack window.

mike_net: fewer long-lived peering links is nice. concerns: AWS route table fragmentation and API quotas if every tenant programs many RTs. what's our mitigation?

liam_arch: mitigation options: 1) per-tenant bridge ENI + aggregated CIDR per-AZ so each tenant only needs a couple of routes, or 2) keep per-tenant mapping at our regional relay and program just a single handoff route in the customer VPC.

sofia_sre: from SRE POV ephemeral instances increase churn. we must ensure reconcilers are idempotent and include backoff/retry with visibility. incidents around teardown races are painful.

nora_product: customers will ask for auditable change trails and guaranteed delivery of logs even if proxy dies. can we stream logs to customer-owned sinks before ack?

liam_arch: proxies will stream audit events to the customer's encrypted S3/CloudWatch using STS creds; we also persist minimal signed audit records to our CP DB for correlation. design ensures logs are encrypted client-side and never in plaintext across our network.

carol_security: threat model: deploying code inside customer accounts expands surface area. limit permissions aggressively (cross-account role with tight policy) and short-lived certs for control-plane comms. also require customers to opt into hosting proxies.

mike_net: IAM policy sketch: allow only Describe/ReplaceRoute on specific RTs, ec2:CreateNetworkInterface limited to allowlisted subnets, plus tag-based scoping. rotate creds frequently and monitor for abnormal API patterns.

liam_arch: certificate options: 1) customer-signed cert using their KMS/HSM, 2) ephemeral cert signed by our CA but provisioned via a customer-approved CloudFormation. pick based on customer's compliance.

sofia_sre: monitoring: expose proxy lifecycle metrics: boot_time_ms, reconcile_duration_ms, route_apply_errors, cert_issuance_failures. index by tenant/region/proxy_id. add an automatic failover: if proxy fails repeatedly, mark tenant to use regional relay path and page on thresholds.

deploy-bot: deploy:liam/edge-lite-proxy v0.1 -> staging 2024-09-04T08:03Z :rocket:

nora_product: onboarding UX: minimize manual steps. propose a single-click CloudFormation approval that creates the cross-account role, with terraform/snippets for infra teams. include a clear FAQ about tradeoffs: latency vs. cost vs. operations.

carol_security: also require customers to provide an allowlist of subnets/RTs the proxy can modify. require an attestation checkbox for hosting code. schedule a brief security review before GA.

mike_net: cost note: lots of small proxies add egress/compute cost and slightly higher tail latency. get a cost model: per-proxy baseline and per-tenant average. good candidate for a later optimization: sleep mode with heartbeat and wake-on-demand.

liam_arch: action items: 1) prototype proxy that programs a single ENI + aggregated prefix, 2) run a 200-tenant API rate test to measure route table API calls, 3) draft narrow IAM policy + CFN flow, 4) create teardown/playbook and idempotency tests.

sofia_sre: I'll own playbook + dashboards. will define SLOs for reconcile time and proxy uptime.

nora_product: I'll write onboarding flow + customer FAQ for expected latency and failure modes.

carol_security: I'll own IAM review and cert rotation plan. want a short code audit for the first spike.

liam_arch: thanks all. will open spike PR with minimal design doc here and schedule follow-up. tentative sync Fri 9am.

mike_net: small HCL sketch for the prototype ENI+route approach:
```hcl
resource "aws_network_interface" "bridge" {
  subnet_id = var.bridge_subnet
  private_ips = [var.bridge_ip]
  tags = { Name = "tenant-bridge" }
}
resource "aws_route" "agg" {
  route_table_id = var.rt_id
  destination_cidr_block = var.aggregated_prefix
  network_interface_id = aws_network_interface.bridge.id
}
```

liam_arch: nice. keep the spike minimal and capture edge cases later. :thumbsup:
